newsitem.title: CANADA: Domco board rejects Armstrong bid.
newsitem.headline: Domco board rejects Armstrong bid.

text.p: Domco Inc said on Tuesday that its board of directors recommended that shareholders reject the takeover bid by Armstrong World Industries Inc.
Domco said its board also decided that the company would not issue new shares as proposed under Armstrong's modified takeover offer.
A unit of Lancaster, Pa.-based vinyl flooring manufacturing rival Armstrong offered on June 6 to acquire all the outstanding shares and convertible securities of Domco Inc at C$23 a share.

Armstrong modified its bid for Farnham, Quebec-based Domco on July 3, making the offer conditional on receiving 51 percent of all shares being tendered on a fully diluted basis. The offer was due to expire on August 15, 1997.
French concern Sommer Allibert, which holds 69.2 percent of Domco's common shares, or 57.1 percent on a fully diluted basis, had said it would not sell its Domco shares to Armstrong.

In its modified offer, Armstrong proposed to subscribe at C$23 a share for a number of newly issued shares, which together with the Domco securities tendered under the offer, would give it 51 percent of Domco shares on a fully diluted basis.
Armstrong is seeking an injunction in a U.S. federal court to block the proposed $565 million merger of Sommer and Tarkett AG, of Germany. Armstrong's request was due to be heard on September 9.

In its court action, Armstrong said it had been in talks with Sommer for more than 12 months on the possibility of combining the two companies' floor-covering operations. Armstrong said it offered on April 17 to buy Sommer's flooring assets, including Domco, for $775 million.
Sommer rejected Armstrong's bid on May 26 and accepted Tarkett's merger offer.
Sommer sued Armstrong in a Quebec court and said it planned similar actions against the company in the United States.

Domco said it had also received on Tuesday a letter from Sommer and Tarkett confirming their intention after the Sommer-Tarkett transaction is completed to combine Domco's businesses with those of Tarkett U.S.
